sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the central part of Tenafly north of the Washington Street business block, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left (the grid is turned about 15 degrees). Central Avenue forms the top edge of the sheet and Washington runs along the bottom, where it is the main commercial row. Tenafly Road runs down the left side, Grove crosses the middle from Central Avenue to Riveredge Road, Chestnut crosses it east to west, and Riveredge Road runs diagonally from the left centre toward the railroad at the lower right. The Erie Railroad's Northern Division occupies the right side: West Railroad Avenue and East Railroad Avenue flank the multiple tracks, with a long coal pocket and freight sheds beside the tracks, and Highwood Avenue appears at the extreme lower right. The north half is a residential district of frame dwellings on narrow lots in blocks 117 and 118, with an auto repair and garage, a cement block making shop and a few stores. In the middle the Tenakill and a tributary brook cross the sheet. Block 119 and block 120 hold the Tenafly Lumber & Supply Co., with a wood working shop, a lumber shed and offices at the railroad side. The south edge of the sheet is lined with stores, a Cement & Cinder Blocks building, an oven and bake shop and apartments facing Washington. Block 121 at the lower left is mostly open ground except the Municipal Building, housing the fire department and police headquarters, with a steel bell tower. Water pipes of six and eight inches run in the streets, with hydrants marked.
notes: Central Avenue is today Central Avenue, Grove is Grove Street, Chestnut is Chestnut Street, Summit Av. (St.) is South Summit Street and Washington is Washington Street in OpenStreetMap.
East Railroad Avenue is Piermont Road in OpenStreetMap; West Railroad Avenue keeps its name.
Printed scale 50 ft to an inch; the fitted scale of 7.85 px per foot agrees.

50 ft, north to the upper left (about -17). Downtown north part: Central Avenue, Tenafly Road, Grove, Chestnut, Riveredge Road, Summit Av (St), Washington, West and East Railroad Avenues; E. Railroad Av is Piermont Road. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the centre of Tenafly's business district south of Washington, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Washington is the street along the top, lined with stores, a dry-goods and drug store block, a bank, a movie theatre and apartments, and at its west end the Public Library. Tenafly Road runs down the left edge, George runs down the middle and Franklin Avenue near the right side, while West Clinton Avenue crosses east to west across the middle of the sheet and meets West Railroad Avenue, the street along the Erie Railroad tracks at the right. The largest feature is Tenafly High School, a brick building with an auditorium and a large block of open school ground on block 123, with a compass rose on the lawn. Tenafly Publishing Co. stands on West Clinton Avenue, and the Tenafly M. E. Church faces the same street on its south side. Below West Clinton Avenue the blocks are mostly frame dwellings with garages on long lots, with the Tenakill Brook crossing block 125 from the upper right toward the bottom. At the right the vacant Richter Mfg. Co. factory and an auto repair garage stand beside Franklin Avenue near the railroad. A pump house, a few stores and the passenger station area appear at the right edge. Force, a street with a culvert crossing, runs along the bottom edge. Six and eight inch water pipes, hydrants and lot numbers are marked.
notes: Written-out forms: West Clinton Avenue is West Clinton Avenue and East Clinton Avenue is East Clinton Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Franklin Avenue is Franklin Street, George is George Street.
Force is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Printed scale 50 ft to an inch.

50 ft, north to the upper left (about -15). Business centre: Washington, West Clinton Avenue, Tenafly Road, George, Franklin Av (Franklin Street), Force (not in OSM); Tenafly High School. No control in the lower half. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the southwest corner of the downtown district and the residential area to the south, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Tenafly Road runs down the left edge, George down the middle of the sheet and Franklin Avenue down the right side, with Westervelt Avenue crossing the lower part diagonally from the lower left to the lower right. Force runs across the top, where it crosses the sheet's upper edge near the Tenakill Brook, which curves from the top centre down the right side and joins the stream beside the Northern Division of the Erie Railroad at the right. The blocks between Tenafly Road and George (block 124) and between George and Franklin Avenue (block 126) are filled with narrow numbered lots holding frame dwellings with garages and sheds, and a few brick-veneered houses. The area south of Westervelt Avenue is blank and carries the number 13, which refers to the neighbouring sheet. At the lower right the W. H. Mowerson Coal & Wood Yard has coal pockets, sheds and a conveyor beside the railroad, and block 127 at the right edge is open land crossed by the brook. A compass rose near the top gives north toward the upper left. Water pipes of six and eight inches, hydrants and the scale bar at lower left are drawn.
notes: Westervelt Avenue is Westervelt Avenue, George is George Street and Franklin Avenue is Franklin Street in OpenStreetMap.
Force is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The OpenStreetMap line of Westervelt Avenue lies 5 to 8 m from the drawn street, so placement uses points carried from sheet 3.
Printed scale 50 ft to an inch.

50 ft, north to the upper left (about -14). Tenafly Road, George, Franklin Av, Force, Westervelt Avenue, Norman Place. Westervelt Avenue lies 5-8 m from its modern line; placed only from 7 points carried from sheet 3, all in the top quarter. Low confidence.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the residential district east of the railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Central Avenue runs along the bottom edge. E. Railroad Avenue runs down the left side beside the Erie Railroad's Northern Division tracks, Harold runs up the left centre from Central Avenue, and County Road runs from the bottom centre up to the top right, with Magnolia Avenue along the right edge. Mahan is the diagonal street at the upper left, with Dale above it and Prospect Ter. at the upper right. The blocks on either side of Mahan (blocks 165 and 166) are cut into very narrow lots, many with frame dwellings and sheds, and a store and an oven are marked among them. The largest building is the Ralph S. Maugham School, a pink brick building with an auditorium at the right of the sheet (block 169). A contractor's yard, W. D. Adams Contractor, with a wagon shed and office stands on Central Avenue at the bottom. The remaining blocks (167 and the area between County Road and Magnolia Avenue) hold scattered dwellings on large lots with blank land around them. Six and eight inch water pipes, hydrants and lot numbers are marked, and a compass rose at the upper right shows north toward the upper left.
notes: East Railroad Avenue is Piermont Road in OpenStreetMap; Prospect Ter. is Prospect Terrace, Mahan is Mahan Street and Harold is Harold Street.
Printed scale 50 ft to an inch; the fitted 8.1 px per foot agrees.
Sheet number 15 appears at the top as a neighbouring sheet.
50 ft, north to the upper left (about -15). Dale, Mahan, Prospect Terrace, County Road, Harold, Central Avenue, East Railroad Avenue, Magnolia Avenue. Detector ink_below_paper 70 for this part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 lies south of Central Avenue and east of the railroad, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Central Avenue crosses the top of the sheet. West Railroad Avenue and East Railroad Avenue run down the left side on each side of the tracks of the Erie Railroad's Northern Division, with Chestnut St. branching to the left of the tracks. County Road runs from the top centre down the middle of the sheet and Highwood Avenue crosses it as a diagonal from the lower left to the right, where it curves to meet Magnolia Avenue at the right edge. Jay is the street at the bottom left and Riveredge Rd. enters at the lower left corner. Laurel Av. joins Magnolia Avenue at the lower right. West of County Road the blocks (block 168 and 171) contain a plumbing shop, a garage and auto repair shop, a filling station, an auto washing shop, a bowling alley and garment factory, coal pockets, hay and feed storage and the S. B. Scales Contractor Yard with long storage sheds. East of County Road the district is largely open ground in blocks 169 and 173. The Tenakill Lodge (a club) and the First Presbyterian Church are drawn at the lower right, and a compass rose at the lower right shows north toward the upper left.
notes: East Railroad Avenue is Piermont Road in OpenStreetMap; Central Avenue, Highwood Avenue, County Road, Magnolia Avenue and Laurel Avenue keep their names; Jay is Jay Street.
The church is lettered Presbyn Church and the club Tenakill Lodge (Club).
Printed scale 50 ft to an inch.
50 ft, north to the upper left (about -14). Central Avenue, Harold, East and West Railroad Avenues, Highwood Avenue diagonal, County Road, Jay, Magnolia, Laurel. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the south part of the downtown area around the railroad station, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. At the left the Erie Railroad's Northern Division runs down the sheet between W. Railroad Avenue and E. Railroad Avenue, with the passenger station drawn on its own platform. Highwood Av. runs south from the top of the sheet along the east side of the tracks and encloses the triangular park (block 178). Jay and the diagonal County Rd. run from the upper centre, with Washington crossing the tracks near the left edge. The district east of County Road is a regular grid of long narrow lots along Hillside Av., which crosses from the centre to the right, New, E. Clinton Av. along the lower part, Valley Pl. and Magnolia Av. and Serpentine Rd. at the right edge. Notable buildings are Our Lady of Mt. Carmel R. C. Church, the parochial school, a post office, a rectory, a lumber and auto repair yard at the top (block 172) and many frame dwellings with garages. The lower left and lower centre are blank paper belonging to neighbouring sheets (19 and 3), with the number 19 printed in the blank area. A compass rose at the right shows north toward the upper left. Water pipes and hydrants are marked on the streets.
notes: East Railroad Avenue is Piermont Road in OpenStreetMap.
The OpenStreetMap lines of New Street (16 to 20 m), Serpentine Road (about 30 m) and the East Clinton Avenue and County Road corner (about 14 m) are displaced from the drawn streets.
Scale 50 ft to an inch is printed; the fitted 8.0 px per foot agrees.

50 ft, north to the upper left (about -11). Jay, Highwood, Railroad Avenues, Washington, County Road, Hillside, East and West Clinton Avenues, New, Serpentine Road, Valley Place, Front. New Street, Serpentine Road and the East Clinton / County Road corner are 14-30 m off their modern lines and were left out. Detector ink_below_paper 70. Medium-low confidence (5 points).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the northwest residential district of Tenafly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the right: Knickerbocker Road runs across the top of the sheet (the west side) and Jefferson Avenue crosses the lower part diagonally. Between them the grid of north-south streets runs across the page: Christie Street at the left, Sunset Lane, Columbus Drive, Newcomb Road, Hickory Avenue, Day Avenue and its continuation Gordon Avenue, with Davenport Avenue at the right edge along the borough limit with Cresskill. Cross streets include Clarke Place, Wight Place, Esmond Place (drawn as a divided street with a central island west of Sunset Lane), Daisy Place, Delany Place, Spruce Street, Esmond Terrace, Washington Terrace and the private Last Road. Most blocks are subdivided into narrow numbered building lots, many still empty in 1930; the built lots carry frame dwellings with private garages, a few brick-veneered or tile houses and one stone dwelling. There are no factories, churches or schools on the sheet. A large open area at the lower left is labelled Athletic Field, and the strip north of Knickerbocker Road at the top is shown only in outline with a few dwellings and a no-exposure note. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes run in most streets, with town hydrants marked. Block numbers run from 34 to 56F. The blank margins refer to sheets 9, 10 and 11, which adjoin to the south and west.
notes: North points to the right of the page (rotation about 93 degrees).
Christie is printed without a suffix; today Christie Street. Spruce is today Spruce Street.
Delany Place is spelled Delaney Place in OpenStreetMap.
Gordon Avenue is printed with the alternative spelling Gordan in parentheses; it continues Day Avenue south of Spruce.
Washington Terrace is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
100 ft. Northwest district between Knickerbocker Road (top, west) and Jefferson Avenue; Christie to Davenport Avenue. North points right (rotation about 93). One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the northwest part of Tenafly along the Cresskill borough line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The borough boundary is lettered along the top left, and Davenport Av. runs below it with Gordon Av. (Gordan Av.), Hickory Av., Newcomb Rd., Columbus Drive and Sunset Lane following in parallel diagonal bands down the sheet. Cortlandt Pl. crosses them near the left, with 5th (printed without a suffix) as a short cross street at the top centre, and Tenakill Brook flows in a curve from the top centre to the bottom, splitting the sheet. West of the brook the blocks are subdivided into very long narrow numbered lots (blocks 40 to 55) with a scatter of dwellings along Newcomb Road and Columbus Drive, greenhouses (Green Ho) and sheds at the middle left, and a large open tract at the lower left marked Athletic Field. East of the brook Cedar, Grove, Mahan and Tenafly Rd. serve a district of narrow lots with the Tenafly Textile Mill (not in operation) and its mill wire, electrical motor and shed buildings (block 116). Central Av. runs along the bottom and W. Railroad Av. runs beside the Erie Railroad at the right edge. Neighbouring sheets 8, 5, 2, 11 and 15 are noted at the margins.
notes: Gordon Av. is printed with the alternative spelling Gordan; today Gordon Avenue.
Cedar is the continuation of Columbus Drive east of the brook in OpenStreetMap; Mahan is West Mahan Street; Grove is Grove Street.
Cortlandt Place and the north end of Cortlandt Pl. are drawn on two offset alignments, so OpenStreetMap's Cortlandt Place was not used as control.
Printed scale 100 ft to an inch.

100 ft, north to the upper left (about -10). Northwest blocks along the Cresskill line: Davenport, Gordon (Gordan), Hickory, Newcomb, Columbus, Sunset, Cortlandt Place, 5th; east of the Tenakill Cedar, Grove, Mahan, Tenafly Road, Tenafly Textile Mill. Control only east of the brook (Cortlandt Place drawn on two offset alignments, left out). Medium-low confidence.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 shows a residential and partly open district of northwestern Tenafly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right of the page. The Borough of Bergenfield limit crosses the top edge. West Clinton Avenue runs down the left side of the sheet, crossed from top to bottom by Morris Road, Jewett Avenue, Browning Avenue, Lyle Avenue and the long Knickerbocker Road, with Cross Street dividing the blocks numbered 14 to 19 north of Knickerbocker Road. Riveredge Road runs down the right-centre of the sheet, bending to the northeast at the top, and Richards runs parallel to it farther right. Blocks between Jewett and Lyle Avenues carry detached frame dwellings with small outbuildings, some blue-tinted for concrete or stone construction; the blocks right of Riveredge Road are cut into very narrow deep lots, mostly empty. South of Knickerbocker Road the sheet is largely open land in large numbered tracts, with a few scattered dwellings, a large house at the left edge, a group of buildings in the lower centre and the compass rose in block 70. At the lower right, H. W. Dreyer's greenhouse range (heated by steam, lighted by electricity) fills block 61, with Wight Place and Esmond Place below it, lined with dwellings. Christie runs down the right edge of the sheet. Block numbers run from 9 to 77 and the left edge carries lettered blocks 20A, 20B, 20H and 20J that continue onto the adjoining sheet. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes run in the principal streets.
notes: North is toward the right of the page (rotation about 94 degrees).
Browning Avenue and Lyle Avenue are today North Browning Avenue / South Browning Avenue and North Lyle Avenue / South Lyle Avenue on either side of West Clinton Avenue.
Richards is today Richard Street; Virginia is today Virginia Street; Christie is today Christie Street; Clarke Place keeps its name.
Cross is not in OpenStreetMap and was not used for control.
Morris Road / Porter Avenue was rejected by the fit (about 8.6 m); Porter Avenue was left out of the street list.
H. W. Dreyer's greenhouses occupy block 61.

100 ft, north to the right (about 94). Knickerbocker Road, West Clinton Avenue, Riveredge Road, Porter, Morris, Jewett, Browning, Lyle, Cross, Richards, Wight and Esmond Places, Christie; Bergenfield line at the top. Porter Avenue left out (8.6 m). One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers a largely open district west of the railroad in the middle of Tenafly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north at the top. Along the top edge, Christie and Virginia run east from Esmond Place, with the ends of Daisy Place and Delaney Place above Christie; the two blocks between Christie, Virginia and Riveredge Road are subdivided into house lots carrying frame dwellings, private garages and one stone-faced house. Jefferson Avenue runs south from Christie past Riveredge Road to West Clinton Avenue. Riveredge Road crosses the whole sheet from Esmond Place to Tenafly Road, curving southeast at its east end. Most of the middle of the sheet, blocks 65, 71, 72, 73 and 77, is undivided open land with only a few buildings, and the Athletic Field reaches into the top of the sheet north of block 65. In the lower right, Tenakill Brook runs north and south between West Clinton Avenue and Riveredge Road; east of it lie Washington and the frontage of Tenafly Road, with dwellings and Grace Chapel, a frame chapel heated by steam and lit by electricity, at the corner of West Clinton Avenue and Tenafly Road. A few dwellings line West Clinton Avenue at the bottom of the sheet. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes run in Riveredge Road, Jefferson Avenue, West Clinton Avenue and Tenafly Road, with hydrants. Figures 2, 3, 8, 9, 10 and 13 at the edges refer to the adjoining sheets.
notes: Christie, Virginia and Washington are printed without a suffix; today Christie Street, Virginia Street and Washington Street.
Grace Chapel at West Clinton Avenue and Tenafly Road.
Jefferson Avenue / West Clinton Avenue was left out: a hand-picked point there was 5 m from the fit to the other nine points.
100 ft, north up. Christie, Virginia, Esmond Place, Jefferson Avenue, Riveredge Road, West Clinton Avenue, Tenafly Road and Washington along Tenakill Brook; mostly open land. One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 lies south of sheet 10 in the northwest part of Tenafly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right of the page. The Borough of Bergenfield limit crosses the top. Knickerbocker Road runs across the sheet from the left edge to the right, dividing a large open tract above it from a developed strip below. North of Knickerbocker Road, Marcotte La. (a private lane) runs down the left of a very large open tract, block 22, holding long sheds, an observatory, two large dwellings and the compass rose; blocks 23 to 25 at the upper left are open land with a few dwellings. At the upper right, Henry, Morris Road, Browning Avenue and Lyle Avenue cross Pleasant Avenue, Floral Terrace and Porter Avenue in small lettered blocks (20A, 20C, 20D, 20E, 20F, 20H, 20J) of narrow lots and detached dwellings; a field of narrow unbuilt lots lies between Pleasant Avenue and Floral Terrace. South of Knickerbocker Road the sheet is cut by Ealedon Road, Sussex Road, Burlington Road, Westervelt Avenue and Norman Place into blocks 81, 82A to 82E and 86 of mostly detached frame dwellings with brick-lined or fireproof outbuildings, and Nassau Terrace crosses between Burlington Road and Westervelt Avenue. Another Westervelt Avenue runs along the bottom edge, with Joyce Road at its lower left. The Knickerbocker Country Club building and the golf links occupy the left edge, and water pipes of six and eight inches run in the principal streets.
notes: North is toward the right of the page (rotation about 93 degrees).
Ealedon Road (Westervelt Avenue), as printed, is today Erledon Road in OpenStreetMap. Henry is today Henry Street.
Browning Avenue and Lyle Avenue are today South Browning Avenue and South Lyle Avenue here.
Knickerbocker Road / Westervelt Avenue was rejected by the fit (about 11 m); Westervelt Avenue is drawn with a bend at that junction.
Junctions along Knickerbocker Road and Norman Place carry residuals of 3 to 5 m because the drawn cross streets are not square to the modern ones.
Nassau Terrace is not in OpenStreetMap.

100 ft, north to the right (about 93). Knickerbocker Road, Ealedon Road (Westervelt Av; today Erledon Road), Sussex, Burlington, Westervelt, Norman Place, Floral Terrace, Marcotte Lane, Henry, Pleasant; Knickerbocker Country Club. Junction residuals 3-5 m; Knickerbocker / Westervelt rejected (11 m). Medium confidence.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 lies south of sheet 12 in the west-central part of Tenafly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right of the page. Westervelt Av. runs along the top edge and the vertical Westervelt Av. runs down the centre of the sheet and then diagonally to the lower left, meeting Tenafly Rd. and George. In the upper half, De Mott Av., Joyce Rd., Sussex Rd., Westervelt Av. and Norman Pl. run down the page, lined with narrow lots of detached frame dwellings in blocks 81 to 88, 87A, 87B and 90; blocks 82, 83, 84, 85 and 87 are cut into long deep lots with sparse building. The Tenakill Brook crosses the sheet from the left edge to the right, passing under Joyce Road, Sussex Road, Westervelt Avenue and Norman Place. A strip of golf links lies at the upper left. Tenafly Rd. crosses the middle of the sheet on a diagonal, with a dense group of dwellings in blocks 128 and 129 on its south side, between Tenafly Ct. and Moller. George runs parallel to it below, and Franklin Av. below that. At the lower left the Tenafly Lumber & Supply Co. occupies block 130 and 131 with a lumber shed, an office, a cement store and lumber piles beside the E.R.R. (Northern Div'n) tracks, with a brook beyond. The compass rose sits at the lower right in block 4, which is largely blank, and the adjoining sheet numbers 3, 4, 14 and 19 mark the neighbouring areas.
notes: North is toward the right of the page (rotation about 90 degrees).
Westervelt Av. along the top edge, between Sussex Road and the vertical Westervelt Avenue, is Palmer Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
De Mott Av. is today Demott Street; Moller is today Moller Street; George is today George Street; Franklin Av. is today Franklin Street; Tenafly Ct. is today Tenafly Court.
Franklin Street / Westervelt Avenue was left out (about 5 m residual); George Street / Moller Street was rejected (about 14 m).
Fitted scale is about 4.07 px per foot, 1.5 percent above the 100 ft expectation.
Tenafly Lumber & Supply Co. occupies blocks 130 and 131 beside the Erie Railroad (Northern Division).

100 ft, north to the right (about 91). Tenafly Road, Joyce, Sussex, Moller, George, Franklin Av, Westervelt (the top-edge Westervelt Av is today Palmer Avenue), Norman Place, De Mott; Tenakill Brook; Tenafly Lumber & Supply Co. Franklin Street left out (5 m); George / Moller rejected (14 m). East third has little control. Fitted scale 4.07 px/ft. Medium-low confidence.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the southwestern edge of Tenafly along the City of Englewood limit, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right of the page. The Englewood boundary, marked City Limits, runs down the left edge. At the upper left, Ivy Lane, Wilkins Pl., Hodskin Pl. and Oak Av. enclose small blocks 102B, 102C, 103 and 94 of detached frame dwellings; a note on the sheet states that these buildings are also shown on the Englewood map. Tenafly Rd. crosses the sheet diagonally from the left edge to the right. North of it, the large open blocks 91, 92 and 93 hold a strip of golf links crossed by the Tenakill Brook, with Hamilton Av., Brook Ter. and De Mott Av. running down from Tenafly Road into narrow deep lots of blocks 92, 92A and 92B. South of Tenafly Rd., Leonard Av., Lindley Av. and De Mott St. run to the southwest in a wedge of closely built dwellings in blocks 134, 135 and 133D, with Franklin St. across the lower part, and George and Franklin Av. at the right. Large open tracts 136, 137 and 138 at the left carry a few scattered buildings and the compass rose. The E.R.R. (Northern Division) tracks cross the lower part of the sheet, with Front beyond them to the south and blocks 190 and 191 largely blank. Six and eight inch water pipes run in the principal streets.
notes: North is toward the right of the page (rotation about 93 degrees).
Hamilton Av. is today Hamilton Place; De Mott Av. and De Mott St. are today Demott Street; Oak Av. keeps its name as Oak Avenue.
Brook Ter. and Franklin St. (west of Lindley Avenue) are not in OpenStreetMap; the printed Franklin Av. near De Mott Street is Franklin Street in OpenStreetMap.
A marginal note reads: These Buildings also shown on Englewood Map.
Oak Avenue / Tenafly Road was not detected because Oak Avenue curves into Tenafly Road.

100 ft, north to the right (about 93). Southwest edge on the Englewood line: Oak Avenue, Hodskin and Wilkins Places, Ivy Lane, Tenafly Road, Hamilton Av (Hamilton Place), Leonard, Lindley, De Mott. One part.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the east side of Tenafly around the Tenakill Brook and the Erie Railroad, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right of the page. Hudson Av. runs down the centre of the sheet, crossed from top to bottom by Atwood Av., Madison Av., Haring Lane, County Rd. and Magnolia Av., and ending at Prospect Ter. at the bottom edge. Prospect Ter. also runs down the left side of the sheet. The right third of the sheet, between Summit and the Borough of Cresskill limit at the right edge, is mostly narrow unbuilt lots in blocks 140 to 146, with Edith, Clark Av., Atwood Av. and Madison Av. crossing them. The E.R.R. (Northern Div.) tracks cross the upper left diagonally, with the Tenafly Sewage Disposal Plant, sand filters and sludge beds beside them, and blocks 109 to 111 and 156 to 159 of narrow empty lots, with Grove (not opened). Hickory Av. and Dale run near the left edge, with Mahan at the far left and Gordon Av. at the top. Between Haring Lane and County Rd. the Samson Granite Co. Inc., manufacturers of concrete blocks, has a large works in block 160 beside Laight, with the Tenakill Brook winding through. Dwellings fill blocks 161 and 162 along County Rd. and Magnolia Av., and a filling station, an auto sales and service garage and scattered houses stand east of Hudson Avenue. Bridge (not opened) runs at the lower right beside a brook. The compass rose is at the left in block 5.
notes: North is toward the upper right of the page (rotation about 52 degrees).
Clark Av. is Jersey Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Summit is North Summit Street; Mahan is Mahan Street.

sheet-16-1.description: The main part of sheet 16 covers the hillside east of Engle Street in the northeast of Tenafly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right of the page. Engle Street curves across the upper part of the sheet, with Prospect Terrace, Orchard Place and Sisson Terrace at the upper left, and Hudson Avenue runs down the middle of the page. East of Hudson Avenue are Knoll (Knole) Road, the oval loop of Union Avenue (Knoll Road), the unopened Bridge and Cliff streets and open land marked No Exposure. Southwest of Hudson Avenue lie Grandview Terrace, Park Street, the private Brook Road and Highwood Avenue, with Glenwood Avenue along the bottom edge. Tenakill Brook crosses the sheet from the top, past a pond beside a greenhouse, under Knoll Road and across Park Street toward Hudson Avenue. The district is one of large suburban lots: frame dwellings, several with stone or tile first stories, a few brick-veneered or tile houses, and private garages and sheds; one estate house at Highwood Avenue is named Grindewald. There is no industry, church or school. Water pipes of six and eight inches run in Engle Street, Hudson Avenue, Knoll Road, Grandview Terrace, Park Street, Brook Road and Highwood Avenue, with hydrants. Block numbers 147, 148, 154, 155, 163, 164, 164A, 197 and 198 appear. A heavy line cuts off the lower right corner of the sheet, where an inset of the Magnolia Avenue district is drawn; references to sheets 15 and 17 mark the adjoining areas.
notes: North is toward the upper right of the page (rotation about 47 degrees).
Engle and Park are printed without a suffix; today Engle Street and Park Street.
Glenwood Avenue is today Glenwood Road.
Union Avenue (Knoll Road), the oval loop east of Hudson Avenue, has no street of that name in OpenStreetMap; the loop is not used for control.
Bridge and Cliff are marked not opened.

sheet-16-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 16 is an inset in the lower right corner of the sheet, cut off from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale of 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing toward the upper right. It shows a small residential district west of Engle Street, near County Road: Magnolia Avenue runs diagonally across the inset, Prospect Terrace meets it at the right, and Sisson Terrace runs down from Magnolia Avenue at the left, turning into Orchard Place, which runs back up to the right; Sisson Terrace continues below Orchard Place at the bottom edge. The block between these streets, numbered 163, is divided into house lots carrying frame dwellings with private garages and one tile dwelling, and a few further houses stand east of Prospect Terrace. Water pipes of six and eight inches run along Magnolia Avenue, Sisson Terrace, Orchard Place and Prospect Terrace, with hydrants. The strip along the heavy line is marked exposure, and the figures 5, 15, 16 and 17 refer to the sheets drawing the adjoining ground. The area lies a short distance northwest of the top left corner of the main map of the same sheet, where Orchard Place and Sisson Terrace are drawn again.
notes: Placed from three points (two detected, Orchard Place / Sisson Terrace hand-picked); a first-order fit with no redundancy, low confidence.

sheet-17-1.description: The main part of sheet 17 covers the residential district east of the railroad around the middle of Engle Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right of the page. Magnolia Avenue runs along the top of the sheet and Hillside Avenue down its left edge; Ravine Road curves from Hillside Avenue to Engle Street, and Laurel Avenue loops down from Magnolia Avenue to Engle Street. Engle Street crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, where Highwood Avenue meets it and continues around the right side of the sheet past Grandview Terrace and Park Street to Glenwood Avenue at the bottom. Edward Court runs south from Engle Street, Forest Road leaves Engle Street toward the bottom of the sheet with Depeyster Avenue off it, and Park Street loops from Forest Road to Highwood Avenue. Sisson Terrace appears at the top right corner. The blocks hold frame dwellings on large lots, many with brick-veneered or tile walls, a few with stone first stories, and private garages. The Church of the Atonement (Episcopal), a tile building lit by electricity and heated by steam, stands on Highwood Avenue near Engle Street. Water pipes of six and eight inches run in most streets, with hydrants. Block numbers include 164, 170, 174 to 177B, 198 and 199. The lower left corner is cut off by a heavy line for an inset, and the ground south of Engle Street at the left and along Forest Road is left to sheet 18; open ground along the lower edge is marked No Exposure.
notes: North is toward the upper right of the page (rotation about 52 degrees).
Engle is printed without a suffix; today Engle Street. Glenwood Avenue is today Glenwood Road.
Church of the Atonement (Episcopal) on Highwood Avenue.

sheet-17-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 17 is an inset in the lower left corner of the sheet, set off from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing up and slightly to the left. It shows a short stretch of Magnolia Avenue, which runs up the left edge of the inset, between Sisson Terrace at the top and Highwood Avenue at the bottom; Orchard Place meets Sisson Terrace at the top, where Sisson Terrace bends away to the upper right. The block between them, numbered 170, carries a few frame dwellings with private garages, one brick-veneered dwelling and one tile dwelling; much of it is open land. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes run in Magnolia Avenue, Sisson Terrace and Highwood Avenue, with hydrants. The figures 5, 6, 16 and 17 in and around the inset refer to the sheets drawing the adjoining ground. The same ground near Orchard Place and Sisson Terrace is also drawn in the inset of sheet 16.
notes: North is up and slightly to the left (rotation about -14 degrees), unlike the main map of the sheet.
Placed from three points (two detected, Orchard Place / Sisson Terrace hand-picked); a first-order fit with no redundancy, low confidence.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 shows a hillside residential district of eastern Tenafly, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right of the page. E. Clinton Av. runs down the left side of the sheet to the Tenakill Brook, where it meets Old Smith Rd., which curves around the bottom of the built area. Engle sweeps across the top in a long curve from the left edge round to Forest Rd. at the right, with Hillside Av. entering from the top edge. Within this frame, Kenwood Parkway (marked Not Opened) and Depeyster Av. run across the middle, and Birchwood Pl. and Mountain Rd. run down from Depeyster Avenue to Old Smith Rd. Forest Rd., also lettered Forest (Old Smith) Rd. along its lower end, encloses the east side of the district and Glenwood Av. leaves it to the right edge. The blocks between Depeyster Av. and Old Smith Rd. (blocks 201, 202 and 203) are cut into regular lots of detached frame dwellings, some with tile or stucco construction in pink, with small garages. The larger blocks 200 and 200A above hold fewer buildings, among them a stone house at the right and a large frame dwelling near the centre. The Tenakill Brook runs through the lower part of the sheet and a second branch crosses at the right. A large dwelling and outbuildings stand on the open land at the left, blocks 19 and 207, and the lower left and bottom are open land in blocks 205 and 206 with scattered buildings. The compass rose is at the upper right, and the sheet edges are marked No Exposure.
notes: North is toward the upper right of the page (rotation about 52 degrees).
Engle is today Engle Street; Hillside Av. is Hillside Avenue; Park is today Park Street.
Glenwood Av. is today Glenwood Road.
Kenwood Parkway is marked Not Opened and is not in OpenStreetMap.
Forest Road / Glenwood Road, Forest Road / Park Street and Engle Street / Forest Road were not detected.
East Clinton Avenue / Depeyster Avenue carries a residual of about 4.7 m.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the southern part of Tenafly west of Engle Street and along the Erie Railroad, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top of the page, tilted slightly to the left. The railroad tracks and the Tenakill Brook run down the left edge. Front runs down the left side beside them, past the Clinton Hotel at the top, a filling station and narrow lots of blocks 182 and 185, to meet Westervelt Av. near the bottom. E. Clinton Av. crosses the top half of the sheet on a diagonal from the upper left to Engle, passing New, Valley Pl. (Rd.), Serpentine Rd. and Hillside Av. Valley Pl. (Rd.), Linden, Huyler Av. and Beach lie in the dense group of dwellings in blocks 183 to 188 at the left, with Westervelt Av. curving across below them and running on a diagonal to Engle at the lower right. Serpentine Rd. runs down the centre of the sheet from Hillside Av. at the top to Westervelt Av. at the bottom, with the large open tracts of block 189 and the lots of block 181 to its right, holding a few large dwellings. Engle forms the right boundary of those tracts and runs down the right of the sheet, with Creston Av. and Coppel Drive leaving it at the lower right into narrow lots of blocks 299, 300 and 301. A large stone or concrete mansion stands at the right edge beside Engle. The lower left is open land in blocks 190 and 191 with a few scattered buildings. The compass rose is at the right.
notes: North is toward the top of the page, tilted to the left (rotation about -11 degrees).
Front is Dean Drive in OpenStreetMap; Valley Pl. (Rd.) is today Valley Place; Linden is today Linden Street; New is today New Street; Engle is today Engle Street.
Beach is not in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-20-1.description: The main part of sheet 20 covers the south end of Tenafly along Engle Street down to the city limits of Englewood, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left of the page. Engle Street runs from the top of the sheet diagonally down to the bottom edge. East of it, North Park Drive and South Park Drive run off Engle Street to Evans Court at the top, and below them Oak and Elm cross Engle Street, with Pine running between them and an unnamed street (today Maple Street) at the right edge; Bliss Avenue leaves Engle Street toward the right in the lower part. West of Engle Street, Serpentine Road runs down the left half of the sheet past Front and the two arms of Hudson Court to Phelps Avenue at the bottom, beside a cemetery and the street car right of way along the left edge. The large open area at the upper left holds the house of Herbert Coppel with a tower nearby. The blocks between Oak and Elm and along Serpentine Road are cut into narrow numbered lots with frame dwellings and private garages; there are greenhouses off Serpentine Road, a workshop on Oak, a large stone house in block 212 and other stone and concrete-block dwellings. Water pipes of six and eight inches run in Engle Street, Oak, Elm, Bliss Avenue, Serpentine Road and Phelps Avenue, with hydrants. Block numbers run from 190 to 212. The upper right corner is cut off by a heavy line for an inset showing Engle Street farther north, and the city limits of Englewood are marked along the bottom edge.
notes: North is toward the upper left of the page (rotation about -37 degrees).
North Park Drive (printed N. Park Drive) is today Woodland Park Drive; South Park Drive (printed S. Park Drive) keeps its name.
Oak, Elm and Pine are printed without a suffix; today Oak Street, Elm Street and Pine Street. The street marked Not Named at the right edge is today Maple Street.

sheet-20-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 20 is an inset in the upper right corner of the sheet, boxed off from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing up and to the left. It shows Engle Street, drawn straight up the inset, north of the area of the main map: Westervelt Avenue meets it from the west at the top, Coppel Drive leaves it to the east just above, Howard Avenue runs east from it in the middle, and North Park Drive leaves it toward the southeast at the bottom. The ground is mostly large open lots in blocks 190, 207 and 301, with a concrete-block dwelling and garages near Coppel Drive, another concrete-block house on Howard Avenue and a few frame dwellings and garages. An eight-inch water pipe runs in Engle Street, with hydrants. The figures 19 and 20 on Engle Street mark where the inset ground passes from the area of sheet 19 to that of sheet 20; the top of the inset repeats the bottom right corner of sheet 19.
